repairs.before: are emergency contributions compensated without converting today's indispensability into unlimited control over the lives and work made possible afterward
repairs.after: is the rescuer's compensation bounded and dated, or does it include open-ended governance rights or a perpetual share of post-rescue output
repairs.why: Fable critic found the initial fairness judgment insufficiently operational
Moved from joint-problem phase to reciprocal commitment

distinctness_note: Necessity leverage at consent and open-ended rescue compensation at settlement are deliberately distinct phases, not two names for one check.

gaps: Actual common-mode losses, beyond common-mode observation error
Affordability conditional on the very states calling for cooperation
Accountability of proxies for principals unable to give instructions
Control over who participates and who may implement an interface
Production, disturbance, confidentiality, and timeliness of monitoring
Activation and attribution before exercising exceptional or punitive authority
gate: list-excellences; open conceptual or phenomenological hypotheses

accepted.item: Common-shock reserve: pooled protection ↔ pooled insolvency — hinge: when the same named shock triggers members’ claims and impairs the pool’s assets, what resources remain available to meet those claims
accepted.why: Separates covariance of real losses and backing assets from Observer independence, which concerns correlated false certification. A pool can have independent auditors and still fail jointly.

accepted.item: Shock-contingent burden: affordable commitment ↔ obligation that peaks as capacity collapses — hinge: under the specified adverse states, do contribution calls adjust to the resources members can still mobilize, or rise precisely when those resources disappear
accepted.why: Participation runway covers the initial bridge to benefit; this covers state-dependent obligations after a feasible entry. Distinct from pool solvency: the pool may remain solvent by bankrupting contributors.

accepted.item: Proxy mandate: represented interests ↔ a representative’s own bargain — hinge: for future people or nonhuman beneficiaries unable to instruct or dismiss a proxy, which beneficiary outcomes constrain the proxy’s decisions and who can challenge a documented departure
accepted.why: Missing-principal ledger asks whether affected interests have a seat or appeal; this asks what binds an occupied seat when its principals cannot discipline it. Does not pretend measured outcomes settle moral status.

accepted.item: Admission control: protective membership rules ↔ incumbents choosing their judges — hinge: can incumbents change eligibility or delay qualified admissions while a decision affecting their own power is pending, without review under the previously applicable rule
accepted.why: Power over entry can determine the deciding electorate despite honest voting and represented outsiders. Distinct from amendment of substantive obligations after sunk costs.

accepted.item: Monitor maintenance: operating verification ↔ an audit nobody sustains — hinge: who bears the cost of collecting and retaining compliance evidence, and does that work continue when certification is least profitable to the parties funding it
accepted.why: Observer independence does not ensure observations continue to exist. This addresses endogenous provision of monitoring effort rather than shared epistemic or financial bias.

accepted.item: Measurement disturbance: informative inspection ↔ inspection that changes the hazard — hinge: do inspection procedures themselves interrupt containment, consume a safety reserve, or induce the behavior whose absence they certify, compared with an otherwise comparable uninspected interval
accepted.why: Inspection footprint concerns capability disclosure; this covers causal disturbance by measurement even when no information escapes. Comparative evidence may be difficult, explicitly not an assurance from an audit label.

accepted.item: Protected contest: confidential verification ↔ an unanswerable secret verdict — hinge: can a challenged finding be examined through a protected procedure with enough detail to contest its decisive inference, without requiring public disclosure of the dangerous evidence
accepted.why: Inspection footprint limits what observers learn; this tests whether secrecy leaves the accused any effective way to challenge an inference. A safe disclosure boundary alone does not provide contestability.

accepted.item: Interface equivalence: interoperable commitments ↔ matching labels with conflicting effects — hinge: when the same permitted action crosses members’ interfaces, do the resulting permissions, units, and obligations match the agreed meaning in an end-to-end demonstration
accepted.why: Acknowledgment depth concerns assent to the same trigger; systems can assent accurately yet implement incompatible translations. A message acknowledgment cannot establish semantic execution equivalence.

accepted.item: Emergency activation: constrained exception ↔ authority that can declare its own necessity — hinge: what evidence must establish the emergency before exceptional powers activate, and can someone other than the beneficiary review that evidence within the action’s useful time window
accepted.why: Emergency sunset tests termination, not whether the exception was legitimately activated. A genuine emergency can warrant action; the hinge does not equate urgent authority with coercion or require delay until ordinary procedure completes.

accepted.item: Breach attribution: discriminating enforcement ↔ inability punished as refusal — hinge: before imposing a defection penalty, does the procedure examine what action the party could perform with the information and resources available at the time
accepted.why: Sanction externality concerns the penalty’s effects and Repair discriminator concerns the cure. This tests the classification that authorizes a penalty; disagreement, incapacity, and intentional refusal are not interchangeable.

accepted.item: Information clock: actionable assurance ↔ certification that arrives after exposure — hinge: does evidence of a violated constraint reach someone able to intervene before the next irreversible joint action, rather than only at the scheduled retrospective audit
accepted.why: Accurate, independent, affordable observation can still arrive too late. Exit bandwidth concerns a party’s withdrawal opportunity, not the coalition’s detection-to-intervention latency.

accepted.item: Protocol ownership: shared interface ↔ a standard whose steward can exclude implementers — hinge: can a conforming independent implementation obtain the specifications, required rights, and certification on the same stated terms as the steward’s own implementation
accepted.why: Interface equivalence asks whether implementations mean the same thing; this asks whether implementation is actually open to another party. Admission control concerns coalition membership, not control of the technical means of participation.

residue.item: Shared-threat realism: common danger ↔ a manufactured enemy — hinge: can parties inspect evidence for the threat independently of the party gaining authority from it
residue.why: Danger contour, Dissent bandwidth, and Observer independence already jointly cover the proposed discriminator; no separate mechanism remains after removing its narrative emphasis.

residue.item: Future seat: intergenerational protection ↔ unborn people omitted — hinge: is anyone authorized to represent those who will inherit the agreement’s risks
residue.why: Direct specialization of Missing-principal ledger. Keep Proxy mandate instead, which exposes failure even when the seat exists.

residue.item: Private proof: bounded disclosure ↔ secrets surrendered for trust — hinge: can compliance be demonstrated without revealing unrelated capabilities
residue.why: Duplicates Inspection footprint; Protected contest retains the different problem of challenging a secret adverse finding.

residue.item: Correlated oracle: many certifiers ↔ one hidden source — hinge: do apparently separate auditors rely on the same upstream evidence
residue.why: Already the deciding observation of Observer independence. Common-shock reserve concerns actual joint losses, not duplicated sources.

residue.item: Contingency account: feasible entry ↔ an unaffordable first contribution — hinge: can a member fund its promised initial contribution before benefits arrive
residue.why: Duplicates Participation runway. Shock-contingent burden instead changes the relevant state after entry.

residue.item: Dissent immunity: cooperation ↔ compelled agreement — hinge: can a member dispute the common forecast without being expelled
residue.why: Dissent bandwidth already protects dissent against removal of evidentiary access; this candidate mainly restates its norm without isolating a new membership mechanism.

residue.item: Portable exit: withdrawal ↔ standards lock-in — hinge: can a departing member move its essential records before access is revoked
residue.why: An implementation of Exit bandwidth, not a new gate. Protocol ownership is retained only for pre-exit implementer exclusion.

residue.item: Mutual trust: credible promises ↔ unsupported confidence — hinge: is there observable evidence that parties will honor their commitments
residue.why: Too generic: it bundles acknowledgment, escrow, monitoring, enforcement, and succession without an independent deciding observation.

limits: Two authored breaths and one independent model gate, not empirical validation or a world novelty search.
Keep rate covers enumerated growth candidates; any extra repair-origin admissions are recorded separately.

gaps: Membership rules can be stable while voting identities multiply under one controller
Represented future claimants can inherit obligations without surviving financial backing
Locally compliant acts and separately compatible agreements can compose into global infeasibility
Constraints may miss delegated execution while interdependence transmits failures
Verification and quorum safeguards need a bounded degraded mode
A recognized shortfall still leaves discretionary power over delivery priorities
gate: list-excellences; open conceptual or phenomenological hypotheses

accepted.item: Constituency dilution: plural representation ↔ one controller multiplying its votes — hinge: can a controller gain decision weight by splitting into nominally independent members without adding a separately accountable interest or contribution
accepted.why: Induced by Admission control: an unmanipulated eligibility rule may still allow one interest to manufacture many qualifying voters. The observation is control-linked splitting, not incumbent discretion over admission.

accepted.item: Liability horizon: deferred protection ↔ harms outliving their backing — hinge: when a protected population’s harm can become observable only after the project ends, what assets and claim process remain available until that interval has passed
accepted.why: Induced by Proxy mandate and Successor binding: beneficiaries can have a faithful representative and a continuing obligation yet no resources when harm matures. This tests duration of backing, not current correlated solvency or identity continuity.

accepted.item: Cumulative exposure: bounded joint risk ↔ individually compliant acts exhausting a shared margin — hinge: are concurrent and repeated permitted actions checked against their combined effect on the agreed safety margin, rather than each being certified against the full remaining margin
accepted.why: Induced by Common-shock reserve and Interface equivalence: agreement on hazards and compatible interfaces does not prevent each participant spending the same finite margin. This is aggregation of permitted activity, not a shock to pooled backing.

accepted.item: Cross-agreement feasibility: compatible alliances ↔ obligations no common action can satisfy — hinge: when two agreements activate together, is there an available action that meets both sets of commitments, or an agreed priority that resolves their conflict
accepted.why: Induced by Interface equivalence: interfaces can translate faithfully while the underlying obligations of overlapping coalitions are logically incompatible. This concerns the feasible action set, not translation errors or unaffordable resources.

accepted.item: Delegation reach: bounded execution ↔ constraints stopping at the signatory — hinge: when a member has a contractor, subsidiary, or agent perform the constrained action, do the same limits and an accountable enforcement path still apply
accepted.why: Induced by Successor binding and Protocol ownership: simultaneous delegation is not replacement of identity or denial of interface rights. A signatory can remain perfectly compliant in its own actions while exporting execution beyond the constraint.

accepted.item: Failure-domain boundary: mutual support ↔ a connection that transmits the initiating failure — hinge: can a failing member be isolated while essential support continues, or does the shared coupling carry its fault into otherwise functioning members
accepted.why: Induced by Common-shock reserve: common external causes and transmitted internal failures differ. Isolation and continued support are observable architectural properties; this is not a prescription to abandon a member or sever every tie.

accepted.item: Degraded-mode authority: resilient coordination ↔ safeguards that disable essential action — hinge: when an expected signer or communication channel is unavailable, does a bounded fallback permit the necessary protective action without silently granting the absent party’s full authority to someone else
accepted.why: Induced by Threshold escrow, Information clock, and Emergency activation: threshold safety can defeat availability even without an emergency declaration. Tests an unavailable-participant path, not whether concessions are released too early.

accepted.item: Scarcity priority: explicit rationing ↔ the controller of delivery choosing who counts — hinge: when resources cannot meet all valid claims, are actual allocations reviewable against a previously stated priority rule, with departures recorded rather than hidden in the delivery queue
accepted.why: Induced by Common-shock reserve and Shock-contingent burden: detecting a shortage and adjusting calls do not determine which valid claims get served. Concerns allocation of actual delivery, not changing eligibility, obligations, or deservingness by fiat.

residue.item: Evidence custody: contestable records ↔ the accused deleting the audit trail — hinge: can a party erase the decisive record after learning that its conduct is challenged
residue.why: Monitor maintenance already includes retention, and Observer independence includes corruption of the input. This version does not yet isolate a third discriminator.

residue.item: Sealed-evidence limit: verifiable restraint ↔ an obligation whose breach cannot safely be proved — hinge: can any authorized protected procedure distinguish compliance from breach without exposing the protected secret
residue.why: An important hard limit, but Protected contest already asks whether decisive inferences can be challenged through a safe procedure. Keep impossibility as a limit rather than count a negated sibling as growth.

residue.item: Monitor reward: evidence production ↔ auditors paid only for favorable findings — hinge: does an adverse finding reduce the monitor’s future compensation or appointment prospects
residue.why: Observer independence explicitly includes incentives; Monitor maintenance covers the provision of effort. A compensation example is not a new category.

residue.item: Audit performance: real compliance ↔ behavior staged for the inspection — hinge: do measured outcomes persist outside the announced inspection window
residue.why: Measurement disturbance already includes behavior induced by inspection. Useful operational example, insufficiently distinct as another gate.

residue.item: Liquid reserve: timely protection ↔ assets unavailable when everyone claims — hinge: can the reserve be converted into the needed support within the joint shock’s deadline
residue.why: Common-shock reserve asks what resources remain available to meet claims; defining availability properly already includes liquidity and timing.

residue.item: Future refusal: durable benefit ↔ descendants unable to reverse the bargain — hinge: can a later generation terminate inherited commitments before dependence makes refusal ineffective
residue.why: Successor binding and Exit bandwidth already supply this discriminator; applying them to descendants is a domain substitution.

residue.item: Proxy replacement: faithful stewardship ↔ a representative who cannot be removed — hinge: can a challenged representative be replaced after documented violation of its beneficiary mandate
residue.why: Proxy mandate includes who can challenge departures. Replacement is one potential remedy, not a separate mechanism at the current grain.

residue.item: Expulsion restraint: accountable discipline ↔ dissent reclassified as grounds for removal — hinge: does an expulsion decision identify a breached commitment rather than only a disputed forecast
residue.why: Breach attribution plus Dissent bandwidth already distinguishes refusal of an obligation from disagreement about a forecast. Do not multiply a named sanction into a new gate.

residue.item: Emergency undoing: temporary response ↔ permanent damage under a temporary power — hinge: which exceptional actions cannot be reversed after the emergency privilege expires
residue.why: Potentially useful prompt, but irreversible protective actions are not inherently defective. It lacks a deciding observation separating justified irreversibility from consumed preconditions; reject rather than equate every emergency loss with abuse.

residue.item: Universal welfare: inclusive cooperation ↔ a bargain that fails to help every being — hinge: does every affected principal end up better off under the arrangement
residue.why: Rejects real tradeoffs by construction and silently invents commensurable baselines for future and nonhuman interests. No feasible universal observation or justified acceptance criterion.

residue.item: Automatic justice: reliable execution ↔ a coded rule that enforces the wrong result — hinge: does the automated rule always implement the morally correct outcome
residue.why: Normative conclusion disguised as a test. The source field contains automated execution, but that does not license an observable universal moral oracle.

residue.item: System perfection: robust alliance ↔ cooperation with any unresolved failure mode — hinge: have all possible breakdowns been ruled out
residue.why: Impossible completeness test. An open diagnostic list cannot certify the absence of unenumerated failures; rejected as the very claim boundary this exercise must preserve.

limits: Two authored breaths and one independent model gate, not empirical validation or a world novelty search.
Keep rate covers enumerated growth candidates; any extra repair-origin admissions are recorded separately.
